requirements.SS-KIT-001: The chart is built from safety.viz's kit on the page: its curves are the kit's `kmEstimate`, the descriptive product-limit estimate, drawn with the kit's Chart.js, bundling neither; without safety.viz on the page it is refused with a message saying what is missing.
requirements.SS-KIT-002: The chart reads no band of the kit's estimate: nothing of its source reads the lower or upper bound or the standard error that `kmEstimate` also returns.
requirements.SS-KIT-003: The chart carries safety.viz's Experimental banner at its top, in the kit's markup and styles, saying its curves are safety.viz's estimator, which awaits its clinical review.
requirements.SS-CFG-001: Every setting has a default; the outcomes table is read by its endpoint, time and one flag, censored (ADaM's CNSR) or event, exactly one named; the groups are a column or a cut variable; a setting that is not known, or a value it cannot take, is refused with a sentence naming it.
requirements.SS-DATA-001: Each participant drawn is in desktop R's group, with R's time and event, for every case: the study by CRP cut at its median, at 4, at its tertiles and at 10, by arm, the women alone, a table flagged by event, and one where an arm has no event.
requirements.SS-DATA-002: The outcomes table is read either way round: a flag of events gives the same participants, groups and curves as ADaM's CNSR, and the flag goes to R as the table gives it.
requirements.SS-DATA-003: A participant with a group and no usable outcome is left out and counted by reason: no row for the endpoint, more than one, a time or flag missing or not a number, a flag that is not 0 or 1, a time below 0; a logical flag is read as R reads one; an outcome row for no such participant is not used, and counted.
requirements.SS-CURVE-001: Each group's curve is the kit's `kmEstimate`, and its steps are R's `survfit()` estimate: the same event times, numbers at risk, events and survival (to 12 decimal places), and the same censored times.
requirements.SS-RISK-001: The at-risk strip counts, at each time of the axis, the participants of a group whose time is at or after it, and a cell lists those participants, the ones R's data hold there.
requirements.SS-RISK-002: On the page, the at-risk strip's counts at each time are R's numbers at risk for each group.
requirements.SS-CUT-001: For a cut variable the histogram holds every value the points were worked out on, and a cut line dropped becomes a typed point as its label writes it, four significant digits; a line cannot pass its neighbour, stop where two points are written alike, or leave the values it cuts.
requirements.SS-HIST-001: On the page, the histogram shows the values the cut points were worked out on, with a line at each point and how many values fall in each group.
requirements.SS-DRAW-001: Event-free survival by CRP at Baseline cut at its median: each group's curve is R's `survfit()` estimate step for step with its censored times marked, the legend gives each group's count, and high CRP has the worse survival, as the study was planted.
requirements.SS-DRAW-002: Groups from a column are drawn by name and a cut at its tertiles makes three curves, low to high, each R's; a column has no histogram.
requirements.SS-DRAG-001: Dragging the cut line moves the curves at once and asks R nothing, and the line says R is asked when it is let go; letting it go makes the cut a typed point as its label writes it, held by the Groups control, and asks R once.
requirements.SS-DRAG-002: Dropped at 4, R's stored answer for the cut at 4 is found and printed, and the curves are R's for that cut; the left and right arrow keys move the line too.
requirements.SS-DRAG-003: An answer asked for before the line was taken hold of is never shown: the line waits for the answer to the cut it is let go at.
requirements.SS-DRAG-004: A click on a cut line, with no drag, leaves it where it is and asks R nothing; a drag moves it by as much as the pointer moves, from where it took hold.
requirements.SS-DRAG-005: Each cut line is a slider of its own, with its value and how far it can go; its arrow keys move it, the curves at once and R once the keys rest; it stops at its neighbours and inside the values.
requirements.SS-STAT-001: R is asked once per view, with one row per participant drawn, and the function, the arguments, the identity and the row count that desktop R's recipe writes; a cut's groups go high to low, so the hazard ratio is the higher group's over the lower's, and a column's in the legend's order; the flag goes under the name the table reads it by.
requirements.SS-STAT-002: Handed to a connection as stored results, each of R's answers is found by the chart's request for its view.
requirements.SS-STAT-003: R's log-rank test is printed with its method and counts, labelled exploratory and unadjusted; each group's median with its log-log interval, in the legend's order, a median or bound R did not reach reading not reached; and, for two groups, the hazard ratio with its interval, a cut's named high over low.
requirements.SS-STAT-004: A hazard ratio R does not estimate is not printed, and R's note says why, as R wrote it (gsm.bio#26).
requirements.SS-STAT-005: A group below R's minimum size prints R's reason and counts, and no number.
requirements.SS-STAT-006: With no R attached the line says statistics are unavailable, the curves are still drawn, and nothing is fetched.
requirements.SS-STAT-007: R's answers stored in the page are found and printed for the women alone, with the filter said, and for a column; a group below R's minimum size prints R's reason.
requirements.SS-STAT-008: On the page, where R does not estimate the hazard ratio it is not printed, and R's note says why.
requirements.SS-STAT-009: Once the connection is replaced, a late answer from the old one changes neither the line nor what `chart.statistics()` reports.
requirements.SS-STAT-010: Where some participants have a value and no outcome, a cut's points are worked out on those drawn, as R's `Analyze_Screen` takes its median: the cut, each group's count and R's answer are desktop R's, and the footnote says who is cut.
requirements.SS-STAT-011: A column's groups are drawn in one order in every browser language, numbers in their names as numbers (2 mg before 10 mg), and R is handed them in the legend's order, so the hazard ratio is the legend's first group's over its second's and names both.
requirements.SS-NEED-001: Loaded without an outcomes table, the chart says it needs one, draws nothing and keeps its controls; given one, it draws; an outcomes table without a column a setting names is refused by name.
requirements.SS-EVENT-001: An outcomes table flagged by event is read the other way round on the page: the same curves, and R is asked with `strEventCol` and finds its answer; `event_col` named alone later, through `setSettings` or `setData`, reads it so too.
requirements.SS-LIST-001: A click on a curve lists its group's participants, and a count of the at-risk strip those it counts, the ones R puts there; a click away from every curve lists nothing, and the legend hides nothing; a row opens safety.viz's participant profile of that participant.
requirements.SS-FAIL-001: When drawing fails the chart says so in its element and keeps its controls, leaving nothing half drawn, and draws again once it can.
requirements.SS-MOBILE-001: At 390 pixels the controls are folded away, the at-risk strip fits or scrolls inside its own box, and the page does not scroll sideways.
requirements.SS-SITE-001: The live demo holds at a 390-pixel-wide viewport with no horizontal scroll, with the controls open; each count of the at-risk strip stays on one line, the strip scrolling in its own box.
requirements.SS-SITE-002: The gallery lists the chart with links to its live demo, its evidence page and its API reference; the demo opens on event-free survival by CRP at Baseline cut at its median, and draws the curves where R cannot be reached and says so.
requirements.SS-SITE-003: The API reference has a table row for every setting the chart has, with the default the code has; the site build fails when one is missing.
requirements.SS-SITE-004: The gallery card and the live demo mark the chart Experimental, with the reason, as the registry gives it, and no other chart is marked.
requirements.SS-LIVE-001: Against R and the survival package started in the browser on the demo: the log-rank p, each median with its interval and the hazard ratio with its interval equal desktop R's within 1 part in 10^8, before and after the cut line is moved to 4.
requirements.SS-LIVE-002: Against R in the browser: by arm, a column, equals desktop R's.
